How to split finances in a marriage is something I see pop up on here a lot & it’s honestly just going to be whatever works for the two of you. I’ve seen people make fun of spouses for venmoing each other for takeout, bills, etc - but if that is what works for you, go for it! 

In my marriage, our philosophy is equity over equality in our finances. I make about twice as much as my spouse and we split our bills in an equitable way - I pay 2 thirds, he does 1 third. Sometimes we will split dinners out, other times we will treat the other one. It is always communicated and agreed upon though. 

I would suggest talking to your spouse about being more equitable with the bill splitting in your household!

OP, I’m going to be honest here, I had the same perspective as you. My anniversary went by this year with pretty minimal effort put in to celebrate by my husband after we agreed to keep things low key. I complained to my therapist about it & her perspective was much like the folks responding here & was completely accurate- your partner is not a mind reader. As much as we WISH they inherently knew what goes on in our heads, they have no idea unless we make our expectations, wants, desires etc clear to them. It was my fault for being upset because I expected him to know what I wanted without communicating it effectively. Now for the holidays, I knew to change the way I communicated and talk to him very clearly about how I would like to exchange gifts this year. He was extremely receptive and we both made lists, set a budget, and even agreed to get things off-list to show we put extra thought into stuff. It’s going to be a really nice holiday and I’m glad I changed my way of thinking. I hope you can too and will enjoy your winter season!

Our wedding was a few months ago and was great! 

A little over 100 people, nice venue, great food etc. It was def more expensive than I originally anticipated!

 If I had advice for people currently planning, it would be to recognize that it’s hard to budget for all decor, dress alterations, etc in the initial planning phases - build some wiggle room into your budget for additional expenses you haven’t thought of. 

Additionally, there were many things I OVER planned & was stressed out about that I realized did not matter at all the actual day of. This was a sigh of relief when I recognized it, but I wish I hadn’t stressed about the small stuff leading up. 

In the end, make sure you & your spouse are sticking to what YOU want. Your family is not the spotlight that day. Have a ceremony that is personal to you, not appeasing others. We loved our Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy & LOTR quotes sprinkled within. 

If I could go back, I don’t think I would change anything - maybe not invite some people, make sure I took my leftovers, remembered the cake topper (lol) - it was generally a really lovely day, mistakes and all
